conflict_resolutions.FULL_AND_PARTIAL_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT: EO 11798 section 1 revokes EO 11796 in its entirety and reserves only accrued violations, which is a savings, not a partial revocation. The partial-amendment reading comes from EO 11810 and EO 11940, which are new orders reissuing materially the same text and do not cite or amend EO 11796; they are recorded as later events and do not revive it.

research_rationale:
EO 11796 (signed 1974-07-30), Continuing the Regulation of Exports, has four clauses (operative lead, sections 1 to 3). Executive Order 11798 (signed 1974-08-14), whose Federal Register text is held, revokes it as a whole in its section 1 except as to violations during the period it was in effect, so every clause ends 1974-08-14. A search of the held corpus for the number of EO 11796 found only EO 11798 and EO 11796's own text; no earlier revocation or Commerce-side end is held. EO 11810 (1974-09-30) and EO 11940 (1976-09-30) are new orders with similar text and are recorded as later events; they do not revive EO 11796.

Export regulations issued by the Secretary of Commerce continued to rest on EO 11533 as continued by EO 11798 section 2.
